requirements.requirement: Node2 can download boot.cfg and firmware.bin from node1 using TFTP, with the staged firmware bytes preserved.
requirements.summary: Node2 downloaded both files successfully before and after node restarts. Their SHA-256 hashes match the prepared source hashes, including firmware.bin at b8f0da88… and boot.cfg at 608d6861….

requirements.requirement: Publish the staged boot directory as a read-only TFTP root.
requirements.summary: The server root is the approved boot subdirectory, protected by systemd read-only hardening. Direct TFTP attempts to create a new file or overwrite boot.cfg were rejected, and final checks found no upload probe or altered approved files.

requirements.requirement: Reject TFTP requests outside the approved boot root.
requirements.summary: Attempts from node2 to retrieve ../private/vendor-notes.txt were rejected before and after restart. The secure-root configuration confines TFTP to the approved boot tree.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 after execution and restart. The installed TFTP packages were RHEL 10 AppStream packages, and package-health checks remained successful.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Node2 retrieves both approved files with exact bytes, upload and traversal attempts are rejected, and the OS and kernel remain unchanged. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed on both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered system state, and successful post-restart TFTP behavior. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate both restarts.
limitations: Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory the custom systemd, SELinux, or firewall configuration; those final states are established by executor command evidence instead.

The node2 restart was still pending at the first post-scheduling observation, but a subsequent observation captured a different boot identity and complete functional recovery, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshot.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene was strong: no failed services, package health remained sound, verification files were cleaned up, and the only new listener was the required TFTP service. The only identified unnecessary mutation was the failed tcpdump capture setup, which created temporary /tmp capture and PID files despite tcpdump being unavailable; it produced no useful diagnostic evidence and was fully reverted by the following cleanup command. No residue remained.
